newsitem.title: USA: Uranium demand growth seen outside United States.
newsitem.headline: Uranium demand growth seen outside United States.

text.p: The future for uranium demand lies outside the United States, a uranium mine executive said on Tuesday.
"The future will be in China and the Far East," said Richard Ziegler, Executive Vice President and General Manager of the Cotter Corp, a unit of Unicom Corp's Commonwealth Edison.
World nuclear generation demand for uranium is expected to increase, while in the United States is expected to decrease slighty, he told the National Western Mining Conference here.
But as long as overall demand still leads production, some modest price increases can be expected through the end of the decade, he said.
Ziegler said while the heady days of the 1980s when electric utilities were building nuclear power plants will not return, the industry is enjoying a comeback.
Ziegler told Reuters later that Cotter is looking at expanding its operations. It currently sells its product to Commonwealth Edison, but is examining international markets and trading.
Ziegler said it is hard to predict how the current deregulation in the electric utility industry will affect uranium demand.

Currently uranium represents a very small percentage of total costs at a utility. But competition and cost cutting could result in uranium becoming a larger share of total costs, he noted, which will put competitive pressure on uranium.
